name: Hungarian verbunkos (military-recruitment dance)
lineage: Hungarian verbunkos military-recruitment dance-music tradition emerging in late-eighteenth century Habsburg-Hungarian military-recruitment practice (the verbunk recruitment-event featured local musicians playing energetic dance-music to inspire young men to enlist). The genre developed canonical compositional conventions: characteristic dotted-rhythm (kuruc rhythm) opening, augmented-fourth Hungarian-Gypsy-scale modal coloring, and characteristic accelerating tempo arc. The verbunkos became the foundational nineteenth-century Hungarian art-music style (informing Franz Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsodies and Béla Bartók's ethnographic-research), and through Brahms's Hungarian Dances entered the broader European musical consciousness. Distinguished from later magyar nóta urban-popular form by verbunkos's late-eighteenth-century historical-recruitment-context origin.
